observations.what_i_see: A concrete farm track ends at a locked gate, and beyond it the ground rises steeply through scrub with no vehicle route visible in any of the frames.
observations.why_it_might_matter: If the holes above the gate are on that slope, plant and rods would have to be carried or a temporary platform built, either of which is a cost that does not appear anywhere in the bill's drilling rates.
observations.corroboration: The station schedule places three holes above the 60 mPD contour on this sheet.

observations.what_i_see: Weathered granite is exposed in the cut face beside the track, with open joints and loose blocks at the toe.
observations.why_it_might_matter: Rock at or near the surface here would mean coring starts early rather than after a soil run, which is a different mode of working from the one a low rock fraction implies.

observations.what_i_see: The flat ground nearest the track is under cultivation, in raised beds with irrigation pipework running between them.
observations.why_it_might_matter: Standing a rig here would need the occupier's agreement and probably reinstatement, neither of which is a drilling cost.

could_not_see: No photograph shows the ground at the far end of the site, so nothing here says anything about the holes on the eastern sheet.
